text: The furnished room received its latest guest with a tired, empty sort of welcome, like the forced smile of someone who had greeted too many strangers. <break time="0.8s" /> A ragged couch and two chairs, a cheap mirror between the windows, and a brass bed stood about, while a bright rug lay like an island on dirty matting. <break time="0.8s" /> On the walls hung the pictures that follow lodgers from house to house, such as The Huguenot Lovers and Psyche at the Fountain, in their tired frames. <break time="0.8s" /> One by one, as if they were witnesses, the marks of earlier tenants appeared, a worn spot in the rug and a stain where a thrown bottle had broken. <break time="0.8s" /> Across the mirror someone had scratched the name Marie with a diamond, as if each tenant had wanted to leave some proof of having once been there. <break time="0.8s" /> The couch had burst its springs and the marble mantel had lost a piece, for people seemed to take out their anger on a home that was never truly theirs. <break time="0.8s" /> From the house came a mix of sounds, a giggle, a scolding voice, the rattle of dice, a lullaby, a banjo, and a cat crying on a back fence. <break time="0.8s" /> He breathed the breath of the house, a damp and musty smell like that of a cellar, mixed with the odors of old linoleum and rotting wood.
